Input: an exercise done at 80 kg x 5 reps. 
 Epley = 80 x (1+5/30) = 93.3 kg; Brzycki = 80 x 36/(37-5) = 90 kg; Lombardi = 80 x 5^0.1 = 94 kg; Mayhew ≈ 95.2 kg; O'Conner = 80 x (1+5/40) = 90 kg. 
 Conclusion: this exercise's 1RM is about 90-95 kg (mid about 93 kg); at 85% intensity the load is about 79 kg.

map.次数越少（≤5 次）估算越准，Epley/Brzycki 在 1–10 次区间常: Fewer reps (≤5) estimate more accurately; Epley/Brzycki are common in the 1-10 rep range. More reps mean larger error; beyond 10 reps, reverse-estimating 1RM is not suggested. Taking the median of multiple formulas is steadier than a single one.
map.为什么不直接测真实 1RM？: Why not test the real 1RM directly?
map.真实 1RM 测试风险高、需充分热身与保护，且神经疲劳大。由亚极限组推算既安全又: A real 1RM test is high-risk, needs full warm-up and a spotter, and causes large neural fatigue. Estimating from submaximal sets is safe and enough to guide loading (e.g. 80% 1RM for strength endurance); beginners especially should avoid frequent max attempts.
